To make *agent-memory* leaderboards commensurable across **budget**, **judge**, and **backbone**, you need to turn “a score” into “a score under an explicitly fixed harness,” and then report *frontier curves* rather than single numbers.

### 1) Fix (and publish) one evaluation harness per benchmark
A core failure mode in memory leaderboards is that rankings flip when papers change the **embedder, reranker, judge model/prompt, or whether baselines are re-run**; the corpus flags this as “eval-config, not architecture” (cmp.agent-memory-systems#analysis). H‑Mem’s re-eval is considered *more comparable* precisely because it forces systems to share key components (paper.hmem-2026#c14), even if it’s not a neutral third party (cmp.agent-memory-systems#verdict).

**Protocol requirement:** for any leaderboard row, the harness must pin and disclose:
- judge model + prompt (and parsing), and any answer “simplification” before scoring (paper.hmem-2026#c14)
- embedder/reranker + retrieval settings
- whether each baseline was **re-run in the same harness** vs copied from other papers (cmp.agent-memory-systems#analysis)

### 2) Normalize across budget by reporting a budget–quality Pareto (not one scalar)
Token budget changes the objective: HORMA explicitly warns its scores are **budget-bounded** (10K/50K) and *not commensurable* with unconstrained leaderboards that also change judges/backbones (paper.horma-2026#limitations). Its evaluation setup makes budget a first-class independent variable and pairs accuracy with token-cost (paper.horma-2026#evaluation_setup).

**Protocol requirement:** report performance as a function of:
- **prompt/context budget** (hard caps, not “no limit” reference rows)
- **#retrieval calls / token-cost**
so comparisons become “who’s better at the same budget” or “who has a better Pareto curve,” not “who has the highest single number.”

### 3) Control backbone effects via stratified leaderboards (or paired deltas)
Backbone changes (manager/agent LLM, retriever LLM) can dominate results; HORMA specifies different roles (manager/agent vs lightweight retriever) and shows capacity constraints matter (paper.horma-2026#evaluation_setup; paper.horma-2026#limitations). So a single mixed-backbone leaderboard is not interpretable.

**Protocol requirement:** either
- run all systems under the **same backbone** (as much as possible), *or*
- publish **paired deltas**: each system’s gain over a shared baseline *within the same backbone tier and budget*.

### 4) Don’t mix judge types; if you must, dual-report
Within one harness, even metric choice can flip winners (noted in the comparison) (cmp.agent-memory-systems#analysis). H‑Mem uses an LLM-judge prompt and also computes F1 after LLM-based simplification (paper.hmem-2026#c14), implying “judge regime” is part of the experimental condition.

**Protocol requirement:** keep one primary judge regime per leaderboard; if reporting multiple (LLM-judge, F1), present them as separate panels, not a merged rank.

Overall: commensurability comes from **(a) one fixed harness**, **(b) budget-indexed reporting (Pareto curves)**, and **(c) backbone/judge stratification**—otherwise you’re comparing different experiments under the same benchmark name (cmp.agent-memory-systems#verdict; paper.horma-2026#limitations).
